cases.statement: Five batch rows; the papers suggest they describe two people (an affected female and an affected female relative in Japanese family F1/'Family 2'/'Family 12'). Both are heterozygous carriers with Behçet-like disease.

phenotype_specificity.statement: Person-level: the features listed for P1/P2 and patient 8 (recurrent fever, oral and genital ulcers, intestinal Behçet's disease, arthritis) are the Behçet-like features the papers describe as typical of HA20. No paper states that other genes were tested and found negative for these people; 40574834 gives only cohort-level methods.

quotes.quote: | P1 | RF negative poly JIA→intestinal BD | + / Paroxysmal | +/+ | + | Poly arthritis | AD | − | Eyelid conjunctival aphthae / Recurrent tonsillitis | Elevated / (4) |
| P2 | PFAPA-like recurrent fever and stomatitis→ intestinal BD | + | +/+ | + | − | − | − | − |  |
Consequently, patients with HA20 present with autoinflammatory Behcet’s disease (BD)-like symptoms and may also develop autoimmune diseases (3).
The diagnosis of HA20 was confirmed via functional analysis of the TNFAIP3 variant.
Genomic DNA was extracted from peripheral blood for sequencing of all exons and exon-intron junctions of *TNFAIP3*.

segregation.statement: Two affected members of family F1 (P1, P2) are both listed with p.W85GfsX in 40574834; the review in 34011076 lists the same family (two affected females, 11 yr and 9 mo onset) but prints the variant only on the first row. Their relationship is not stated in the text (it is shown only in the pedigree figure, whose layout did not survive text conversion). No unaffected relatives' genotypes are stated. Cohort-level penetrance figure quoted for context.

quotes.quote: | F1 | P1 | F | 10 yr | p.W85GfsX | NSAIDs, colchicine, MTX, TCZ | PSL, IGU, ADA | (7,8) |
| F1 | P2 | F | 9 mo | p.W85GfsX | Colchicine | PSL | (7,8) |
Additionally, family analysis revealed that three cases with heterozygous variants were asymptomatic (penetrance: 95.7%).

functional.statement: No assay of c.252delC is reported in these papers. 40574834 says its reporter assay covered newly identified variants and excluded known variants; c.252delC in family F1 is cited to earlier reports (refs 7, 8), so it was probably not re-tested, but the text does not say so explicitly.

quotes.quote: To confirm the pathogenicity of newly identified *TNFAIP3* variants, excluding cases of large deletions and known variants, nuclear factor (NF)-κB-driven luciferase reporter gene assays employing A20-deficient HEK293 cells were performed, as previously described (2).

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Single-nucleotide deletion causing a frameshift, predicted p.(Trp85GlyfsTer11) (from the batch HGVS). Disease mechanism as stated in the papers: heterozygous loss of function (haploinsufficiency).

quotes.quote: A20 haploinsufficiency (HA20) is a hereditary autoinflammatory disease caused by heterozygous loss-of-function variants in the TNFAIP3 gene (1).
A20 haploinsufficiency (HA20) is a systemic autoinflammatory disease caused by a heterozygous loss-of-function mutation in the TNF-α-induced protein 3 (TNFAIP3).

authors_classification.statement: Cohort-level only: 40574834 calls all 35 variants in its cohort 'pathogenic'; 36211342 says the HA20 patients' variants included 'previously reported variants'. No per-variant ACMG criteria.

quotes.quote: All 54 patients analyzed had heterozygous variants in TNFAIP3, comprising a total of 35 distinct pathogenic variants.
Determination of the patients’ genotypes and TNFAIP3 variants revealed several previously reported variants (32)

concerns: Likely duplicate people across identities: HA20-ID0709 (40574834 P1), HA20-ID0218 (36211342 patient 8) and HA20-ID0586 / HA20-ID0584 (34011076 Family 2 and Family 12) are probably one person. Evidence: 40574834 P1 and 36211342 patient 8 share the initial diagnosis 'RF negative poly(articular) JIA → intestinal BD', and 40574834 cites reference 4 (= 36211342) for P1's IFN score; 34011076 lists the same family twice, once cited to Kadowaki et al. and once to Ohnishi et al., which are the two references (7, 8) 40574834 gives for family F1.
Age at onset differs between reports for the probable same person: 10 yr (40574834 P1) vs 11 yr (34011076, 36211342).
Carriers not in the batch: the second (9-month-onset female) row of 34011076 Family 2 and of Family 12 has no variant printed in its own row; these are probably 40574834 P2 (HA20-ID0720).
34011076 is a review table without case descriptions; it cites the original reports (Kadowaki 2018, Ohnishi 2017), which are not in the batch.
40574834 writes the protein as p.W85GfsX in Supplementary Table 1 and as p.Trp85GlyfsX11 in the pedigree figure; no transcript is named in any of the three papers.
notes_for_panel: Evidence is mostly one Japanese family (two affected females) reported in at least three papers. No variant-specific functional data, segregation counts or population data are stated in the batch papers; the original family reports (Kadowaki 2018, Ohnishi 2017) are cited but were not provided.
